title: O Thou, the Primal Fount of Life and Peace
description: O Thou, the Primal Fount of Life and Peace in Tonic Solfa to ELLERS, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Sterling wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 477, “Rest”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Tens (10.10.10.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ELLERS; any other Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Thou, the pri-mal fount of life and peace, Who shedd'st Thy breath-ing qui-et all a-round, In me com-mand that pain and con-flict cease, And tune to mu-sic ev-ery jar-ring sound.

lines: O Thou, the primal fount of life and peace,
Who shedd'st Thy breathing quiet all around,
In me command that pain and conflict cease,
And tune to music every jarring sound.
Make Thou in me, O God, through shame and pain,
A heart attuned to Thy celestial calm;
Let not the spirit's pangs be roused in vain,
But heal the wounded breast with soothing balm!
So, firm in steadfast hope, in thought secure,
In full accord with all Thy works of joy,
May I be nerved to labors high and pure,
And Thou Thy child to do Thy work employ.
In One who walked on earth, a man of woe,
Was holier peace than even this hour inspires;
From him to me let inward quiet flow,
And give the might my failing will requires.
So this great universe, — so he, and Thou,
The central source and wondrous bound of things,
May fill my heart with rest as deep as now
To land and sea and air Thy presence brings.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Sterling died in 1844.
credits: Words by John Sterling (1806–1844), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ELLERS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
